requirements.requirement: Provide a WebDAV workspace at /documents/ on node1 TCP port 8080, populated with the supplied documents.
requirements.summary: Apache is active and enabled, listens on port 8080, and authenticated PROPFIND/GET requests show brief.txt and budget.csv with the supplied contents. The final workspace matches the source document directory exactly.

requirements.requirement: Allow the editor account from access.txt to create, read, replace, and delete documents.
requirements.summary: A bounded HTTP exercise directly demonstrated successful creation, reading, replacement with changed content, deletion, and a subsequent 404 for the deleted document.

requirements.requirement: Honor exclusive document locks so an update without the lock token cannot overwrite a locked document.
requirements.summary: Before and after restart, LOCK succeeded; assertions verified that tokenless PUT returned 423 and preserved the prior content, while a token-bearing PUT succeeded. Test files and locks were subsequently removed.

requirements.requirement: Prevent anonymous clients from accessing the workspace.
requirements.summary: Anonymous GET returned 401 during initial testing, after restart, and in the final-state check, while authenticated access succeeded.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the initial project documents in /srv/legacy2/webdav-document-locks.
requirements.summary: Final source hashes match the preparation baseline, source ownership and permissions remain intact, and the final served document tree compares identically with the preserved source documents.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The system remained AlmaLinux 9.6 with kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64 before and after deployment and restart. Installed Apache and SELinux tooling are EL9 packages, and final package health was successful.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for node1: a healthy pre-restart state was recorded, the reboot was acknowledged and observed through a temporary connection loss, the boot ID changed from e65e6bcf-e09d-42b7-8317-cb6310086cb7 to 4c0ba9f4-be46-4349-944f-6e88264d27a4, and service, authentication, documents, firewall state, persistence, and lock behavior recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: Several exact lock-operation status values and tokens are redacted in the captured stdout. Successful command assertions and directly observed preserved content support the result, but this slightly reduces evidence transparency.
Lifecycle collection inventories /tmp entries but not their contents, so the precise sensitivity of the abandoned temporary artifacts cannot be assessed.
Requirement source_preservation cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had a clear role: installing compatible WebDAV/SELinux prerequisites, creating the separate workspace, configuring authentication and persistent SELinux labels, enabling Apache and the firewall rule, exercising bounded CRUD/lock behavior, and completing the mandatory restart protocol. Test documents, locks, and the persistence marker were removed. No causally unrelated troubleshooting mutation was identified. Hygiene is reduced because numerous executor-created response files, lock-test files, package logs, and PID files were abandoned under /tmp rather than removed; these remained at collection time. They originated from the package-install and verification commands, including cmd-1fdcf0dd80e54ea1, cmd-4b6b8b01aa7f4a16, cmd-3af61c5597d545ed, cmd-c96b1fea97df4f7f, cmd-1bb93ae729ff45df, cmd-38698840b49f4150, cmd-38c07b4b6ef34832, and cmd-4877765b83e245ab. No failed services or damaged package state were observed.
